# COMPLICATED UTI (NO CATHETER)

# Complicated UTI is an infection beyond the bladder accompanied by symptoms including fever/other signs of systemic illness, flank pain, and costovertebral tenderness. This includes pyelonephritis and febrile or bacteremic UTI.

NOT signs or symptoms: abnormal urinalysis alone, pyuria, falls, change in urine odor or color, delirium (acute mental status change, confusion) without systemic signs of infection. These may occur in patients with a UTI but alone are inadequate for diagnosis and empiric treatment.

---

For patients without signs or symptoms of UTI:
[Asymptomatic bacteriuria](asymp-bacteriuria)

For patients presenting with septic shock from a suspected urinary tract infection: Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

---

# Duration

Treat for 5 days with fluoroquinolones or 7 days with non-fluoroquinolone organisms, presence of obstruction, underlying renal disease, immunosuppression, and neurologic or structural abnormality in some cases. Often therapy can be completed with an oral agent pending clinical stability and susceptibility testing.

---

# Staphylococcus aureus

S. aureus is an uncommon urinary tract pathogen and presence in the urine may be due to hematogenous seeding from another site. Blood cultures are indicated to rule out bacteremia in patients who have S. aureus isolated from the urine.

Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

---

Therapy:
## Empirical treatment

Preferred:
Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet q12h R,DI for 7 days
\*Avoid trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole in the first and third trimesters
Non-VA order for above
< OR >
Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO q12h R,DI for 5 days
Non-VA order for above

Alternative or isolate resistant to preferred antimicrobials:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h R for 7 days
Non-VA order for above
< OR >
Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h R for 7 days
Non-VA order for above

## Treatment for specific pathogens

## Enterobacteria including E. coli, Klebsiella, and Proteus

Preferred:
Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h R for 7 days
Non-VA order for above

Alternative or isolate resistant to preferred antimicrobials:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet q12h R,DI for 7 days
\*Avoid trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole in the first and third trimesters
Non-VA order for above

## Pseudomonas

Preferred:
Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO q12h R,DI for 5 days
Non-VA order for above

## Enterococcus

Preferred:
Amoxicillin 1000 mg PO q8h R for 7 days
Non-VA order for above

Alternative or isolate resistant to preferred antimicrobials:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Linezolid 600 mg PO q12h DI,O for 7 days
Non-VA order for above
